# Button Counter (Knopenteller; previously Buttons / Knopen tellen; also Counting Buttons)

> A tool for your financial future. Enter your age, savings and monthly budget and see the chance your money lasts, based on 4,000 simulations. For 11 countries, no account.

Button Counter is a free, single-page retirement calculator at https://countingbuttons.com. It runs entirely in the browser, needs no account and stores what you enter only on your own device. It is a general calculation tool and does not give financial advice.

## Pages

- [How long will your savings last? See your financial future | Button Counter (English)](https://countingbuttons.com/): A tool for your financial future. Enter your age, savings and monthly budget and see the chance your money lasts, based on 4,000 simulations. For 11 countries, no account.
- [Hoe lang gaat je spaargeld mee? Zie je financiële toekomst | Knopenteller (Nederlands)](https://countingbuttons.com/nl/): Rekentool voor je financiële toekomst en eerder stoppen met werken. Vul je leeftijd, spaargeld en maandbudget in en zie de kans dat je geld genoeg is, op basis van 4.000 simulaties.
- [Wie lange reicht Ihr Erspartes? Ihre finanzielle Zukunft im Blick | Button Counter (Deutsch)](https://countingbuttons.com/de/): Rechner für Ihre finanzielle Zukunft. Alter, Erspartes und Monatsbudget eingeben und sehen, mit welcher Wahrscheinlichkeit Ihr Geld reicht. Auf Basis von 4.000 Simulationen.
- [Combien de temps durera votre épargne ? Votre avenir financier en vue | Button Counter (Français)](https://countingbuttons.com/fr/): Simulateur pour votre avenir financier. Indiquez votre âge, votre épargne et votre budget mensuel et voyez la probabilité que votre argent suffise, sur la base de 4 000 simulations.
- [¿Cuánto durarán tus ahorros? Mira tu futuro financiero | Button Counter (Español)](https://countingbuttons.com/es/): Calculadora para tu futuro financiero. Introduce tu edad, tus ahorros y tu presupuesto mensual y mira la probabilidad de que tu dinero alcance, con 4.000 simulaciones.

- [Was ist mein Geld in einem anderen Land wert?](https://countingbuttons.com/de/rente-im-ausland/): Vergleichen Sie die Kaufkraft Ihres Monatsbudgets in 31 europäischen Ländern und prüfen Sie Ihren Plan mit den Regeln von zehn Ländern. Ohne Konto.

- [¿Cuánto vale mi dinero en otro país?](https://countingbuttons.com/es/jubilarse-en-el-extranjero/): Compara el poder adquisitivo de tu presupuesto mensual en 31 países europeos y prueba tu plan con las normas de diez países. Sin cuenta.
- [How much do I need to retire?](https://countingbuttons.com/how-much-do-i-need-to-retire/): It differs per person. It depends on your monthly budget, the age you stop working, your Social Security or State Pension and the tax on your investments. Button Counter combines them and shows the savings you need for your money to last in 9 out of 10 scenarios.
- [How long will my money last?](https://countingbuttons.com/how-long-will-my-money-last/): It depends on your monthly withdrawals, your pensions, your investments and inflation. Button Counter shows year by year how your savings develop and the chance that they last.
- [Can I retire at 62?](https://countingbuttons.com/can-i-retire-at-62/): It depends on your savings, your monthly budget and the lower Social Security benefit you get at 62. Enter the benefit your statement shows for that age and set your stopping age to 62. Button Counter shows the chance that your money lasts.
- [Is the 4% rule still safe?](https://countingbuttons.com/is-the-4-percent-rule-safe/): As a rough guide, yes. It ignores Social Security or a State Pension, tax on your returns and how long your own retirement lasts. Button Counter adds those and shows a monthly amount with the chance that your money lasts.
- [Does the 80% rule work?](https://countingbuttons.com/80-percent-rule-retirement/): A common guide is about 80% of what you earned before. Your real number depends on your housing costs, health care and plans. In Button Counter you enter the monthly budget you want and see whether it holds.
- [How much do I need for $1,000 a month in retirement?](https://countingbuttons.com/1000-a-month-rule/): About $240,000 if you withdraw 5% a year, or $300,000 at 4%. What you really need depends on your other income, tax and how long the money has to last. Button Counter works it out for your situation.
- [I started saving late. Can I still catch up?](https://countingbuttons.com/started-saving-late/): No. Even with fifteen years to go, a fixed monthly amount adds up, next to Social Security or a State Pension. In Button Counter you tap plus on what you set aside and see what it adds to your monthly income later.
- [Is the State Pension enough to live on?](https://countingbuttons.com/is-the-state-pension-enough/): The full new State Pension is about £12,550 a year in 2026/27. That is just under what the Retirement Living Standards call a minimum lifestyle for one person (£13,900). Button Counter shows how much your workplace pension and savings need to add for the budget you want.
- [Can I live on Social Security alone?](https://countingbuttons.com/can-i-live-on-social-security-alone/): The average retirement benefit is about $2,070 a month in 2026. Compare your own benefit with the monthly budget you want. Button Counter shows how much your savings need to add and the chance that they last.
- [Am I on track for retirement in my 40s?](https://countingbuttons.com/am-i-on-track-for-retirement/): Compare what you will be able to spend each month later with what you want to spend. Button Counter works that out from your savings, what you set aside each month and your expected pension, and shows what an extra amount or a different stopping age changes.
- [How much should I save each month for retirement?](https://countingbuttons.com/how-much-should-i-save-for-retirement/): It depends on your goal and your timeline, not on one rule. In Button Counter you set what you put aside each month and see what it adds to what you can spend later, next to your pension and Social Security or State Pension.
- [Should I save or invest for retirement?](https://countingbuttons.com/save-or-invest-for-retirement/): Over long periods, investments have usually grown more than savings accounts, with ups and downs along the way. Button Counter shows what different mixes could mean for your monthly income later, so you can see the difference for yourself. It is not financial advice.
- [Hoeveel geld heb ik nodig om te stoppen met werken?](https://countingbuttons.com/nl/hoeveel-geld-nodig-om-te-stoppen-met-werken/): Dat verschilt per persoon. - [Hoe tel ik mijn pensioen mee in mijn FIRE-doel?](https://countingbuttons.com/nl/pensioen-meetellen-in-fire/): Vul in wat je pensioen per maand oplevert en vanaf welke leeftijd. Knopenteller rekent vier mixen voor je door en laat per mix zien hoeveel je later te besteden hebt en hoe groot de kans is dat je je doel haalt. Het is geen advies; het laat het verschil zien.
- [Klopt de 4%-regel ook in Nederland?](https://countingbuttons.com/nl/4-procent-regel-nederland/): Als ruwe vuistregel wel, maar hij mist je AOW, je pensioen en de belasting in box 3. Knopenteller rekent die mee en laat zien hoeveel je per maand kunt uitgeven, met de kans dat je geld het volhoudt.
- [Vervroegd pensioen: wat kost één jaar eerder stoppen?](https://countingbuttons.com/nl/een-jaar-eerder-stoppen/): Meer dan één jaar aan uitgaven, omdat je ook een jaar minder inlegt en je geld een jaar langer mee moet. In Knopenteller verschuif je je stopleeftijd met plus en min en zie je meteen wat het met je maandbudget doet.
- [Laat begonnen met pensioen opbouwen: heeft het nog zin?](https://countingbuttons.com/nl/laat-beginnen-met-sparen/): Ja. In Knopenteller tik je op plus bij wat je opzij legt en zie je meteen wat het later per maand oplevert.

Button Counter führt diese Punkte zusammen und zeigt, welches Vermögen Sie brauchen, damit Ihr Geld in 9 von 10 Fällen reicht.

Button Counter zeigt Jahr für Jahr, wie sich Ihr Vermögen entwickelt, und wie groß die Chance ist, dass es reicht.

In Button Counter erhöhen Sie Ihren Sparbetrag und sehen sofort, was das später pro Monat bringt.

Button Counter réunit ces éléments et montre le capital nécessaire pour que votre argent tienne dans 9 cas sur 10.

Button Counter montre l’évolution de votre capital année après année et la probabilité qu’il suffise.

Button Counter montre année par année ce qui rentre et ce que votre capital doit couvrir, et la probabilité que votre argent suffise.

Même avec quinze ans devant vous, un montant fixe par mois compte, en plus de vos pensions. Dans Button Counter, vous augmentez votre versement et voyez aussitôt ce qu’il apporte par mois plus tard.
- [Montant de ma pension : est-ce suffisant ?](https://countingbuttons.com/fr/pension-legale-suffisante/): Comparez-la au budget mensuel que vous visez. Button Counter montre ce que votre pension complémentaire et votre épargne doivent ajouter, et la probabilité que cela tienne.

Button Counter lo reúne y muestra el ahorro necesario para que tu dinero aguante en 9 de cada 10 casos.
- [¿Cuánto me durará el dinero en la jubilación?](https://countingbuttons.com/es/cuanto-me-durara-el-dinero/): Depende de lo que retires al mes, de tu pensión, de tus inversiones y de la inflación. Button Counter muestra año a año cómo evoluciona tu patrimonio y la probabilidad de que sea suficiente.
- [Jubilación anticipada: ¿puedo jubilarme antes de los 67?](https://countingbuttons.com/es/jubilarme-antes-de-los-67/): Sí, si tus ahorros cubren los años hasta que empiece tu pensión. Button Counter muestra año a año lo que entra y lo que tiene que salir de tus ahorros, y la probabilidad de que el dinero aguante.
- [¿Funciona la regla del 4 % en España?](https://countingbuttons.com/es/regla-del-4-por-ciento-espana/): Como orientación, sí. Pero no incluye tu pensión pública, los impuestos sobre tus ganancias ni lo que dure tu propia jubilación. Button Counter los incluye y muestra lo que puedes gastar al mes.
- [¿Cuánto debo ahorrar al mes para la jubilación?](https://countingbuttons.com/es/cuanto-ahorrar-al-mes-para-la-jubilacion/): Depende de tu edad, tus ahorros actuales, tu objetivo y tu pensión. En Button Counter cambias tu ahorro mensual y ves al instante lo que supone más adelante.
- [Vivir de rentas: ¿cuánto dinero hace falta?](https://countingbuttons.com/es/vivir-de-las-rentas/): Depende de tus gastos, de tu edad y de la pensión que cobrarás más adelante. Button Counter muestra si tu patrimonio alcanza, antes y después de que empiece tu pensión.
- [Empezar a ahorrar a los 40 o 50: ¿llego a tiempo?](https://countingbuttons.com/es/empezar-a-ahorrar-tarde/): No. Incluso con quince años por delante, una cantidad fija al mes se nota, además de tu pensión pública. En Button Counter subes tu ahorro mensual y ves al instante lo que añade más adelante.

## Questions and answers

### What is Button Counter?

Button Counter gives you a view of your financial future: how long your savings will last and what changes when you adjust something. You enter your age, your savings and what you want to spend each month. Button Counter then shows the chance that your money lasts until your end age, based on 4,000 simulations of good and bad market years.

### Why Button Counter instead of a simple calculator?

A simple calculator answers one sum, such as how long an amount lasts or how much tax you pay on savings. Button Counter puts everything in one plan: your savings, your pension and state pension, work per period, one or two people and the rules of your country. Instead of one number you see the chance that your money is enough, based on 4,000 simulations. Every number shows whether it comes from a source, is an assumption or was entered by you.

### How much savings do I need to stop working?

That depends on your monthly budget, your age and the pension you will receive. Button Counter calculates the amount you need for a 90% chance that your money is enough. As a rough rule of thumb, people often need 25 to 30 times the yearly spending that their pensions do not cover.

### How is the chance of success calculated?

Button Counter runs 4,000 simulations in which returns go up and down each year. It does this for four mixes (defensive, balanced, aggressive, and savings without investing), after costs, tax and inflation, so every amount is in today’s money. The chance of success is the share of simulations in which your money lasts until your end age. Two crash scenarios, one like 2008 and one like 2022, are shown separately.

### Does my spending stay the same in the calculation, or does it fall?

You choose this under “How does your spending develop later?”. With Flat, your spending stays the same every year, in today’s money. That is the most cautious choice, and it is free. Research in several countries shows that people spend differently in different stages of life. With Pro you can plan with such a pattern. Under each option you see how much you need, so you can see what the choice makes of a difference. These are averages: your own spending may develop differently.

### Which countries does Button Counter support?

Button Counter has its own rules for the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, France, Spain, Italy, Portugal, Ireland, the United Kingdom and the United States, plus a general setting for other countries. Each country has its own state pension, pension age and tax on investments. Button Counter also compares what your budget is worth in 31 European countries, based on Eurostat price levels.

### Is Button Counter free, and what happens to my data?

Button Counter has no advertising and needs no account. Most of it is free and stays free; a few extended features are closed off on purpose as Pro. What you enter stays in your own browser on your own device and is not sent to Button Counter. Visits and the use of features are counted anonymously, without cookies.

### Is this financial advice?

No. Button Counter is a general calculation tool that gives estimates based on simplified rules and assumptions. It does not give advice about your personal situation. Check official sources and consult an independent, licensed adviser before you make important financial decisions.

### How much money do I need to retire?

It differs per person. It depends on your monthly budget, the age you stop working, your Social Security or State Pension and the tax on your investments. Button Counter combines them and shows the savings you need for your money to last in 9 out of 10 scenarios.

### How long will my savings last in retirement?

It depends on your monthly withdrawals, your pensions, your investments and inflation. Button Counter shows year by year how your savings develop and the chance that they last.

### Can I afford to retire at 62?

It depends on your savings, your monthly budget and the lower Social Security benefit you get at 62. Enter the benefit your statement shows for that age and set your stopping age to 62. Button Counter shows the chance that your money lasts.

### Does the 4% rule still work?

As a rough guide, yes. It ignores Social Security or a State Pension, tax on your returns and how long your own retirement lasts. Button Counter adds those and shows a monthly amount with the chance that your money lasts.

### How much of my income will I need in retirement?

A common guide is about 80% of what you earned before. Your real number depends on your housing costs, health care and plans. In Button Counter you enter the monthly budget you want and see whether it holds.

### How much savings do I need for $1,000 a month?

About $240,000 if you withdraw 5% a year, or $300,000 at 4%. What you really need depends on your other income, tax and how long the money has to last. Button Counter works it out for your situation.

### Is it too late to start saving for retirement at 50?

No. Even with fifteen years to go, a fixed monthly amount adds up, next to Social Security or a State Pension. In Button Counter you tap plus on what you set aside and see what it adds to your monthly income later.

### Can you live on the State Pension alone?

The full new State Pension is about £12,550 a year in 2026/27. That is just under what the Retirement Living Standards call a minimum lifestyle for one person (£13,900). Button Counter shows how much your workplace pension and savings need to add for the budget you want.

### Is Social Security enough to retire on?

The average retirement benefit is about $2,070 a month in 2026. Compare your own benefit with the monthly budget you want. Button Counter shows how much your savings need to add and the chance that they last.

### How do I know if I am on track for retirement?

Compare what you will be able to spend each month later with what you want to spend. Button Counter works that out from your savings, what you set aside each month and your expected pension, and shows what an extra amount or a different stopping age changes.

### How much should I save per month for retirement?

It depends on your goal and your timeline, not on one rule. In Button Counter you set what you put aside each month and see what it adds to what you can spend later, next to your pension and Social Security or State Pension.

### Is it better to save or invest for retirement?

Over long periods, investments have usually grown more than savings accounts, with ups and downs along the way. Button Counter shows what different mixes could mean for your monthly income later, so you can see the difference for yourself. It is not financial advice.

## Facts

- Method: Monte Carlo simulation, 4,000 runs, three portfolios (defensive, balanced, aggressive), after costs, tax and inflation; all amounts in today's money.
- Headline result: the chance that savings last until the end age, and the capital needed for a 90% chance.
- Countries with their own rules: Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, France, Spain, Italy, Portugal, Ireland, United Kingdom, United States; plus a general setting.
- Purchasing power comparison: 31 European countries, Eurostat price levels.
- Languages: English, Dutch, German, French, Spanish.
- Price: most of it is free and stays free; a few extended features are Pro. No advertising. No account.
